zh: 基尔大学，位于英国中部斯塔福德郡纽卡斯尔安德莱姆附近的基尔村，距离特伦特河畔斯托克约5英里（3公里），是一所英国公立研究式校园大学. 大学原为创办于1949年的北施他佛郡大学学院，并于1962年获英女皇颁发皇家特许状，升格为大学. 基尔为英国二次大战后第一所新成立的平板玻璃大学，致力于推广跨学科研究，是英国大学中提供双学位课程的先驱. 基尔大学占地250公顷，为英国最大的校园大学（Campus University）. 学校大部份学科都在校园里上课，惟基尔大学医学院则在附近位的北施他佛郡大学医院里为医科生提供诊所和病理实习机会.
大学的创办源自林斯男爵（Alexander Dunlop Lindsay）的愿景，作为牛津大学贝利奥尔学院的院长，他认为大学应该更加普级，并关心基层人士接受高等教育的机会. 林斯男爵于1925年在北施他佛郡工人教育协会中演讲，并首次提出建立一所「平民大学」（people's university）的愿景.
1946年，林斯男爵去信时任英国大学资助委员会主席莫利爵士（Walter Moberly），表示有意创立一所新型大学. 得到的回复却是大学资助委员会只赞成新开办的学院成为伦敦大学的一所附属学院，并颁发伦敦大学的遥距学位. 但林斯男爵认为新建立的大学应该拥有颁授学位的权力，但资金可以有意见成立的大学资助. 为此，林斯男爵曾向牛津大学校长请求赞助.
后来，史笃城市议会成立了一个委员会，探讨在施他佛郡成立一所大学的可能，并得到市议员贺活（Thomas Horwood）的支持. 1949年，委员会获得大学资助委员会批出资金，并从善德家族（Sneyd）手中购买了一所宏伟的大宅基尔堂和邻近善德庄园的土地，北施他佛郡大学学院正式成立. 善德庄园与二战期间曾被英国陆军征用作为军营，英军撤退后留下大量平房，成为大学创办初年的课室和宿舍.
基尔大学的第一任校长为 Lord Lindsay of Birker，从1949年到1952年.
en: Keele University is a public research university in Keele, approximately 3 mi from Newcastle-under-Lyme, Staffordshire, England. Founded in 1949 as the University College of North Staffordshire, it was granted university status by Royal Charter as the University of Keele in 1962.

Keele occupies a 625 acre rural campus close to the village of Keele and includes extensive woods, lakes and Keele Hall set in the Staffordshire Potteries. It has a science park and a conference centre, and is the largest campus university in the UK. The university's Medical School operates the clinical part of its courses from a separate campus at the Royal Stoke University Hospital. The School of Nursing and Midwifery is based at the nearby Clinical Education Centre.

Cambridge and Oxford extension lectures had been arranged in the Potteries since the 1890s, but outside any organised educational framework or establishment. In 1904, funds were raised by local industrialists to support teaching by the creation of a North Staffordshire College, but the project, without the backing of Staffordshire County Council, was abandoned.

By the late 1930s, the Staffordshire towns of Longton, Fenton, Burslem, Hanley had grown into the largest conurbation in the UK without some form of university provision. A large area including Staffordshire, Shropshire and parts of Cheshire and Derbyshire did not have its own university. Stoke, in particular, demanded highly qualified graduates for the regional pottery and mining industries and also additional social workers, teachers and administrators. A. D. Lindsay, Professor of Philosophy and Master of Balliol College, Oxford, was a strong advocate of working-class adult education, and suggested a "people's university" in an address to the North Staffordshire Workers' Educational Association in 1925.

Recently appointed to the House of Lords, Lindsay participated in producing the influential Foreign Office report University Reform in Germany, which argued that no institution deserved the name of "university" unless it combined teaching and research. Consistent with his democratic ideals of education, Lindsay also warned of the dangers of training the specialist intellect in the natural sciences and the need to introduce elements of social sciences at university level by broadening the academic agenda. Lindsay believed technological excesses sponsored by the state without a review of the social and political consequences had been a major contributor to Germany's downfall. This was to heavily influence Keele's curriculum.
